title: model-catalog: add listing filters, compatibility flags, and pricing/limits to capability endpoints
author: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Extend the model catalog capability endpoints to support richer listing filters, explicit compatibility flags (including OpenAI-compat mapping), and pricing/limits metadata used by the API surface and SDKs. Motivation: downstream customers and SDKs need first-class signals about compatibility (openai, redwood-structured-output, tool-calling), per-model pricing and token/throughput limits, and filterable model listings so runtime routing and client SDKs can make correct choices without relying on ad-hoc heuristics. What this PR does: 1) Adds new query params to GET /models: 'capability', 'compatibility', 'max_price_cents', 'min_tokens', 'region' to enable server-side filtering. 2) Extends the /models/:id and /models/:id/capabilities payloads with optional fields: 'compatibility_flags' (array), 'pricing_info' (map of currency->price_cents), 'limits' (max_sequence, max_throughput_tpm), and 'structured_output' boolean. 3) Introduces a compatibility mapping layer that marks models as 'openai_compatible' when they satisfy a defined subset of APIs/behaviors; this powers the OpenAI-compat endpoint and SDK autoselect. 4) Adds server-side validation and a migration to backfill capability rows for curated models. 5) Stabilizes streaming chunks emitted from capability endpoints to avoid out-of-order partial updates (fixes a flaky client observed in e2e tests). 6) Updates OpenAPI spec, SDKs (Python/TS), and example docs. Backwards compatibility: All new fields are optional and additive. Clients that ignore unknown fields continue to work. The compatibility flags are additive and do not change existing identifiers; the legacy 'openai_compat' query param is preserved as an alias. Performance: Filtered listing is implemented in the DB layer with indexed columns for common filters (compatibility_flags, region, pricing tiers). Added integration test coverage and a brief load test showing ~2% p95 latency overhead on cold catalog queries; acceptable within current SLOs. Checklist: - [x] API design and OpenAPI schema - [x] Backend handler + DB migration - [x] Compatibility mapping implementation - [x] Streaming stability fixes and test coverage - [x] SDK changes (Python/TS) and examples - [x] Docs: API reference + migration notes - [x] Load/perf check and CI green Migration notes: run migrations/20260211_add_model_capability_fields.sql before deploying the API service. Clients should be updated to tolerate new optional fields; SDKs include a compatibility shim for older runtimes. Tests: unit tests for handler logic, integration tests for end-to-end listing and compatibility filters, and streaming stability tests added. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the compatibility mapping rules in pkg/compat/openai_compat.go and the streaming chunk ordering changes in pkg/streaming/stream_stability.go. The PR intentionally keeps pricing as integer cents to avoid floating point rounding in clients. Related: ENG-2456 (model routing), ENG-2499 (streaming stability), PM-102 (model catalog product requirements).

release_notes: Model catalog: new listing filters (capability, compatibility, price, tokens, region)
Capability payloads include compatibility_flags, pricing_info, and limits (max_sequence, max_throughput_tpm)
OpenAI compatibility mapping added to model metadata; SDKs updated to expose compat flags
Streaming stability improvements for capability endpoints to prevent out-of-order partials
migration_notes: Run migrations/20260211_add_model_capability_fields.sql before deploying the API. New fields are optional. Ensure SDKs are updated to accept the additional optional fields and the compatibility flags enum.
notes_for_ops: Deploy order: migrate DB -> deploy catalog service -> deploy SDK releases. Backfill script included scripts/compat_map_generator.py. Monitor catalog-db for index hot spots; follow-up ENG-2508 created.
